thread:
jordan: Hey all — Jordan here, starting on runtime today. Trying to build the runtime from source (main @ latest) and hitting a ptxas arch mismatch during nvcc compile. Anyone seen this before?

jordan: Build log snippet:
```
[ 12%] Building CUDA object ...
ptxas fatal   : Value 'compute_80' is not recognized for option '--gpu-name'
nvcc fatal   : Unknown option 'ptxas'
```

jordan: I have CUDA 12.1 + driver 535.54 installed on my laptop, and CUDNN 9.1. LD_LIBRARY_PATH seems correct. Trying to build with docker image `nvidia/cuda:12.1-devel-ubuntu22.04`.

mika: welcome! :wave:
mika: That ptxas error usually means nvcc is invoking an older ptxas in PATH. run `which ptxas` and `ptxas --version`.

jordan: `which ptxas` returns /usr/local/cuda/bin/ptxas and `ptxas --version` -> bundled with cuda toolkit shows 12.1

eli: Try `nvcc --version` too. Also check if you have cuda-toolkit from distro and cudatoolkit conda package conflicting.
eli: We saw similar where `apt install nvidia-cuda-toolkit` produced an incompatible ptxas earlier.

jordan: nvcc shows 12.1, but build inside docker still fails. It seems the image has `/usr/bin/ptxas` from the distro package.

runtime-bot: CI Job #1428 failed: runtime/build-linux-gpu (ptxas mismatch). See https://ci.redwood.dev/1428 

mika: In container, check `/usr/bin/ptxas` symlink. Sometimes distro packages put one earlier in PATH. Try `update-alternatives` or remove the distro package and use CUDA toolkit bin.

eli: Also confirm the gcc used inside container. NVCC embeds arch flags; on A100 we tend to target sm_80. Our CMake uses `sm_80` not `compute_80` for nvcc flags — mismatch can surface as ptxas errors.

jordan: Ok I removed `nvidia-cuda-toolkit` inside the container and rebuilt — progress. Now hitting `undefined reference to cublasLt` during link.

mika: That one means you need link flags: `-lcublasLt -lcublas -lcudart`. In our CMake we conditionally add cublasLt when CUBLASLT_FOUND. Run `ldconfig` and ensure libcuBLASLt.so present in /usr/local/cuda/lib64.

olivia: Also check that `CUDA_HOME` and `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` point to the toolkit in the image and not to distro libs. If you want a dev GPU in-house, ping infra for `dev-gpu-queue`.

dev-platform: @jordan I can grant access. Send me your corporate email and I'll add you to the `dev-gpu-queue` group. Also there is a `runtime-onboarding.md` in the repo with these pitfalls documented.

jordan: Thanks all — removing distro toolkit fixed ptxas, adding cublas link fixed the linker. I just added a short note to the onboarding doc about the `nvidia-cuda-toolkit` pitfall and the container PATH gotcha.

mika: Nice, thanks for updating the doc. CC me + @eli on the PR and include the container diff.

jordan: Will do. Appreciate the quick help :heart:
